utterances.speaker: YVES TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbian Radical Party supported the Serbian Democratic Party of the Serb Republic of Krajina, the SDS and the branch of its party created in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Therefore, the intentions of the Serbian Radical Party was not to compete in electoral or political terms with those parties because it felt that these organisations were defending the Serbian national cause very well, so they were allies and supporters amongst themselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Are you aware -- aware of instances where Dr. Seselj met with Radovan Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: YVES TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That happened. I can't remember exactly when but there were meetings.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: What is Dr. Karadzic's relation to the SDS?

utterances.speaker: YVES TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were relations that were developed in the context of the war. At the time, the Serbian Radical Party was extending military support by sending volunteers to Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Can you describe some of the political and ideological similarities between Dr. Karadzic and Dr. Seselj?

utterances.speaker: YVES TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One cannot say that there was an agreement regarding the creation of a state that would assemble all the Serbs. In that they were agreed, but on the ideological level there were differences, because in 1991, 1992, Radovan Karadzic did not exclusively refer to the traditions of the Ravna Gora Movement.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: What did Dr. Karadzic advocate with regard to the non-Serb population in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: YVES TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The wish of the Serbian Democratic Party of Bosnia and Herzegovina was to create a Serbian entity within Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: And with regard to the non-Serb civilian populations, were they included in that?

utterances.speaker: YVES TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One has to state that the non-Serb population was chased out from numerous locations within that entity that is Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Let me ask you to look at 65 ter number 237, and in the interest of time this is another reprint from a book by Dr. Seselj. It's an interview of him for ON magazine entitled "Chetnik revenge will be blind." Dr. Seselj reprinted it in his book, "Politics as a challenge to the conscience." Does this document appear to be as I've described it?

utterances.speaker: YVES TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Have a P number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number P155.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Looking at the text of the interview, it appears the journalist asked Dr. Seselj about having met with Radovan Karadzic while he was in Pale.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think that the Prosecutor should give us the date of that interview, because there's no point discussing the contents if we don't know the date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. What is the date, madam, please, if you have it.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: I believe the interview was May 24, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: If we turn to the last page of the reprint can you indicate, Mr. Tomic, who the journalist was, the newspaper and the publication date of the interview?

utterances.speaker: YVES TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the journal ON, and its issue of the 24th of May, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Did Dr. Seselj indicate the position with respect of the Serbian Radical Party vis-a-vis the policies of the Serbian Democratic Party in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: YVES TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He mentions the meeting with Radovan Karadzic during his visit to Bosnia-Herzegovina, and the Chetnik command is set up in the region of Romanija, and he mentions a meeting with the Chetnik commander in this region, which is east of Sarajevo, but I don't see the point regarding his position. He keeps repeating his intention of amputating part of Croatian territory.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAHL
utterances.text: Let me turn your attention to the answer to the second question at the beginning of the interview. I believe it's on page 58 of the Serbian text, that starts "I already scheduled some rallies in Sarajevo," and it continues on to describe his meeting with Radovan Karadzic. Does he indicate whether the Radical Party supports the policies of Dr. Karadzic's party?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have another general objection. You have probably noticed almost all day today the Prosecutor is dealing with documents which are not relevant for the indictment period. If this doesn't bother you, it doesn't bother me at all, certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but I think the Prosecutor has to set a basis. It is time to finish. Mr. Witness, you were asked a precise question. Will you please answer it? Would you read the sentence, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The letters are very small, and I am having problems with reading it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps it will be best that we come back to this issue tomorrow. Madam, I think we -- I thought we could have finished with you today, but you have another 35 minutes left tomorrow. We will begin with you tomorrow, and after that Mr. Seselj will start his cross-examination. So we will meet again tomorrow at 8.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 31st day of January, 2008, at 8.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.16 p.m.,
